title.zh: 卷74 列傳第39 酷吏
title.raw: 卷74 列傳第39 酷吏 Volume 74 Biographies 39: Cruel Officials

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十四列傳第三十九

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 74, Biography 39
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, 74th year of Volume, 39th year of Biography

sentences.zh: ○酷吏

translations.literal: ○ Cruel Officials
translations.idiomatic: Cruel Officials

sentences.zh: 夫為國之體有四焉：一曰仁義，二曰禮制，三曰法令，四曰刑罰。

translations.literal: The structure of governing a state has four aspects: first, benevolence and righteousness; second, ritual and institutions; third, laws and ordinances; fourth, punishments and penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The foundations of statecraft are fourfold: benevolence and righteousness, ritual and institutional order, laws and ordinances, and punishments and penalties.

sentences.zh: 仁義禮制，政之本也，法令刑罰，政之末也。

translations.literal: Benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and institutions are the root of governance; laws, ordinances, punishments, and penalties are the branch of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and propriety form the root of government; laws, ordinances, and criminal sanctions are its branches.

sentences.zh: 無本不立，無末不成。

translations.literal: Without the root it cannot stand; without the branch it cannot be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Without the root, governance cannot stand; without the branches, it cannot be brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 然教化遠而刑罰近，可以助化而不可以專行，可以立威而不可以繁用。

translations.literal: Yet transformative teaching is distant while punishments are near; they can assist transformation but cannot be practiced exclusively, can establish authority but cannot be used frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Yet moral instruction works slowly while punishments take immediate effect. Punishments may reinforce teaching but must not replace it; they may establish authority but must not be applied incessantly.

sentences.zh: 《老子》曰：「其政察察，其人缺缺。」

translations.literal: Laozi says: "When government is penetrating, the people are deficient."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, "When government is overly scrutinizing, the people grow defective."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「法令滋章，盜賊多有。」

translations.literal: He also says: "When laws and ordinances multiply, thieves and bandits become many."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When laws proliferate, thieves and bandits multiply."

sentences.zh: 然則令之煩苛，吏之嚴酷，不能致理，百代可知。

translations.literal: Thus when ordinances are burdensome and onerous, and officials are severe and cruel, they cannot bring order—it is known through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus burdensome edicts and cruel officials cannot bring good order—a truth evident across the ages.

sentences.zh: 考覽前載，有時而用之矣。

translations.literal: Examining past records, there have been times when they were employed.
translations.idiomatic: A review of earlier histories shows that such measures were sometimes employed.

sentences.zh: 昔秦任獄吏，赭衣滿道。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin employed prison clerks, and convicts in ochre robes filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Qin entrusted power to prison officials, until the roads swarmed with prisoners in ochre garb.

sentences.zh: 漢革其風，矯枉過正。

translations.literal: Han reformed this custom, correcting the deviation by overshooting.
translations.idiomatic: The Han revised this practice, but in correcting the excess they swung too far the other way.

sentences.zh: 禁網疏闊，遂漏吞舟，大奸巨猾，犯義侵禮。

translations.literal: The prohibition net became loose and broad, so that even a ship-swallowing fish leaked through; great villains and cunning scoundrels violated righteousness and encroached upon ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The penal net grew so lax that even great offenders slipped through; powerful criminals and cunning rogues violated duty and trampled ritual.

sentences.zh: 故剛克之吏，摧拉凶邪，一切禁奸，以救時弊，雖垂教義，或有所取焉。

translations.literal: Therefore officials of firm suppression crushed and pulled down the vicious and wicked, prohibiting all wickedness entirely to save the ills of the age—though they transgressed teaching and righteousness, something might be taken from them.
translations.idiomatic: Hence stern, hard-driving officials who shattered wickedness and banned all corruption to remedy the disorders of their day—though they often trampled proper teaching—sometimes had something to recommend them.

sentences.zh: 高祖膺期，平一江左，四海九州，服教從義。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu received the mandate, pacified the lands south of the Yangtze, and throughout the four seas and nine provinces all submitted to teaching and followed righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu assumed the throne, he unified the south of the Yangtze, and throughout the realm the people submitted to moral instruction and observed proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 至於威行郡國，力折公侯，乘傳賦人，探丸斫吏者，所在蔑聞焉。

translations.literal: As for those whose authority ran through commanderies and kingdoms, who bent dukes and marquises by force, who rode the post relays to levy men and who carried pellets to strike down officials—nowhere were such heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Those who lorded it over commanderies and kingdoms, who bent nobles by force, who rode the courier relays to extort the people, and who carried pellets to ambush officials—such figures were nowhere to be found.

sentences.zh: 無曩時之弊，亦已明矣。

translations.literal: That the abuses of former times were absent was already clear.
translations.idiomatic: The absence of the abuses of earlier ages was already plain.

sentences.zh: 士文等功不足紀，才行無聞，遭遇時來，叨竊非據，肆其褊性，多行無禮，君子小人，咸罹其毒。

translations.literal: Shiwen and the like had achievements insufficient to record, conduct and talent unheard of; encountering the opportune time, they presumptuously usurped unfitting positions, indulged their narrow natures, and often acted without propriety—gentlemen and petty men alike suffered their poison.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Shiwen had no achievements worth recording and no reputation for talent or conduct; they merely seized an opportune moment and usurped posts they did not deserve. They indulged their narrow tempers and habitually acted without propriety, and both gentlemen and commoners alike suffered at their hands.

sentences.zh: 凡厥所蒞，莫不懍然。

translations.literal: Wherever they governed, none failed to tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Every place they governed was filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 居其下者，視之如蛇虺，過其境者，逃之如寇仇。

translations.literal: Those beneath them regarded them as serpents and vipers; those who passed through their territory fled as from bandit enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates looked on them as serpents and vipers; travelers who entered their jurisdictions fled as from mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 與人之恩，心非好善，加人之罪，事非疾惡。

translations.literal: When they showed others favor, their hearts were not inclined to goodness; when they heaped guilt on others, their affairs were not born of hatred of evil.
translations.idiomatic: When they showed favor, it did not spring from a love of goodness; when they piled on guilt, it did not spring from a hatred of wickedness.

sentences.zh: 其所笞辱，多在無辜，察其所為，豺狼之不若也。

translations.literal: Those whom they flogged and humiliated were mostly innocent; examining their conduct, they were worse than wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those they beat and humiliated were innocent; judged by their actions, they were worse than wolves.

sentences.zh: 無禁奸除猾之志，肆殘虐幼賤之心，君子惡之，故編為《酷吏傳》也。

translations.literal: They had no will to prohibit wickedness and eliminate scoundrels, but indulged hearts cruel and abusive toward the young and lowly; gentlemen hated them, and therefore they are compiled in the "Biographies of Cruel Officials."
translations.idiomatic: They had no wish to root out corruption, only to indulge cruelty toward the weak and humble. Men of principle despised them, and for this reason they are gathered in the Biographies of Cruel Officials.

sentences.zh: ○厙狄士文

translations.literal: ○ Yuku Di Shiwen
translations.idiomatic: Yuku Di Shiwen

sentences.zh: 厙狄士文，代人也。

translations.literal: Yuku Di Shiwen was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuku Di Shiwen was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖幹，齊左丞相。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gan was Left Chancellor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gan served as Left Chancellor of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父敬，武衛將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Martial Guard General and Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was Martial Guard General and Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 士文性孤直，雖鄰里至親莫與通狎。

translations.literal: Shiwen was solitary and upright by nature; even with close neighbors and kin he would not associate familiarly.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Shiwen was aloof and upright; he would not socialize even with close neighbors and relatives.

sentences.zh: 少讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he studied books.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied the classics.

sentences.zh: 在齊襲封章武郡王，官至領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the office of Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu and rose to the post of Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，山東衣冠多迎周師，唯士文閉門自守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, the gentry of Shandong mostly welcomed the Zhou army; only Shiwen shut his gates and held himself aloof.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, the gentry of Shandong largely welcomed the Zhou armies, but Shiwen alone shut his gates and held himself apart.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，授開府儀同三司、隨州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at this and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the privilege of an independent establishment, and Governor of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment, and Governor of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加上開府，封湖陂縣子，尋拜貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo County, and soon after appointed Governor of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shiwen was further promoted to Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo, and soon appointed Governor of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 性清苦，不受公料，家無餘財。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and austere; he would not accept public provisions, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in austere integrity, refused his official stipend, and kept no surplus wealth at home.

sentences.zh: 其子常啖官廚餅，士文枷之於獄累日，杖之一百，步送還京。

translations.literal: His son often ate cakes from the official kitchen; Shiwen put him in the cangue for many days, beat him one hundred strokes, and sent him on foot back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his son ate cakes from the official kitchen, Shiwen had him shackled in prison for days, beaten a hundred strokes, and sent on foot back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 僮隸無敢出門，所買鹽菜，必於外境。

translations.literal: Servants dared not go out the door; whatever salt and vegetables were bought had to be purchased outside the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: His servants dared not step outside the gate; even salt and vegetables had to be bought beyond his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 凡有出入，皆封署其門，親舊絕跡，慶吊不通。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone went in or out, he sealed and signed the door; relatives and friends were cut off, and congratulations and condolences were not exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Every coming and going was sealed and signed on the door; kin and friends were shut out, and no visits for joy or mourning were permitted.

sentences.zh: 法令嚴肅，吏人股戰，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Laws and ordinances were stern and solemn; clerks and people trembled in their legs, and nothing lost on the road was picked up.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were severe and solemn; officials and commoners trembled with fear, and no one picked up lost property in the streets.

sentences.zh: 有細過，必深文陷害。

translations.literal: For minor faults he invariably twisted the letter of the law to entrap people.
translations.idiomatic: Even for trifling faults he invariably twisted the law to entrap people.

sentences.zh: 嘗入朝，遇上置酒高會，賜公卿入左藏，任取多少。

translations.literal: Once he entered court and encountered the emperor holding a high feast with wine; the emperor granted the dukes and ministers entry to the Left Storehouse to take as much as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he attended court the emperor was holding a grand banquet and granted the nobles entry to the Left Storehouse to take whatever they wished.

sentences.zh: 人皆極重，士文獨口銜絹一匹，兩手各持一匹。

translations.literal: Others all took to the utmost; Shiwen alone held one bolt of silk in his mouth and one bolt in each hand.
translations.idiomatic: Others loaded themselves to the utmost; Shiwen alone carried one bolt of silk in his mouth and one in each hand.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，士文曰：「臣口手俱滿，餘無所須。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; Shiwen said: "My mouth and hands are both full; I need nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Shiwen said, "My mouth and hands are both full—I need nothing more."

sentences.zh: 上異之，別加賞物，勞而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by this, gave him additional rewards separately, consoled him, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished, gave him additional gifts, commended him, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 士文至州，發擿奸隱，長吏尺布升粟之贓，無所寬貸。

translations.literal: When Shiwen reached his province, he exposed hidden wickedness; even a foot of cloth or a dipper of grain in bribes from senior clerks he would not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: At his province Shiwen ferreted out hidden wrongdoing; even the smallest bribe from senior clerks he would not forgive.

sentences.zh: 得千餘人而奏之，上悉配防嶺南，親戚相送，哭泣之聲遍於州境。

translations.literal: He obtained more than a thousand persons and memorialized them; the emperor assigned them all to garrison Lingnan; relatives saw them off, and the sound of weeping filled the whole province.
translations.idiomatic: He uncovered more than a thousand offenders and reported them; the emperor sent them all to garrison Lingnan. As relatives escorted them off, weeping filled the province.

sentences.zh: 至嶺南，遇瘴癘死者十八九，於是父母妻子唯哭士文。

translations.literal: Reaching Lingnan, eight or nine in ten died of miasma; then fathers, mothers, wives, and children wept only for Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingnan eight or nine in ten died of pestilence; then parents, wives, and children wept only against Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 士文聞之，令人捕捉，撾捶盈前，而哭者彌甚。

translations.literal: When Shiwen heard of it, he had people seize and beat them until the front was filled with flogging victims, yet the weeping grew still louder.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiwen heard of this he had people seize and beat them until the ground before him was covered with victims, yet the weeping only grew louder.

sentences.zh: 有京兆韋焜為貝州司馬，河東趙達為清河令，二人並苛刻，唯長史有惠政。

translations.literal: There was Wei Kun of Jingzhao as Beizhou Assistant Administrator, and Zhao Da of Hedong as Qinghe Magistrate—both were harsh, and only the Chief Clerk practiced benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kun of Jingzhao served as Beizhou Assistant Administrator, and Zhao Da of Hedong as Qinghe Magistrate—both were harsh, while only the Chief Clerk showed benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「刺史羅刹政，司馬蝮蛇瞋，長史含笑判，清河生吃人。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "The governor's yaksha government, the assistant's viper glare, the chief clerk's smiling judgment, Qinghe's raw man-eating."
translations.idiomatic: People of the day said, "The governor's demon rule, the assistant's viper glare, the chief clerk's smiling verdict, Qinghe's raw man-eating."

sentences.zh: 上聞而歎曰：「士文之暴，過於猛獸。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and sighed: "Shiwen's ferocity surpasses fierce beasts."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and sighed, "Shiwen's brutality surpasses that of savage beasts."

sentences.zh: 竟坐免。

translations.literal: In the end he was removed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was dismissed from office for it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以為雍州長史，士文謂人曰：「我向法深，不能窺候要貴，必死此官矣。」

translations.literal: Before long he was made Chief Administrator of Yongzhou; Shiwen told others: "My law enforcement has been deep; I cannot fawn on the powerful and noble—I am sure to die in this office."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Chief Administrator of Yongzhou. Shiwen told others, "I have enforced the law too strictly and cannot court the powerful—I am sure to die in this post."

sentences.zh: 及下車，執法嚴正，不避貴戚，賓客莫敢至門，人多怨望。

translations.literal: When he descended from his carriage, he enforced the law sternly and correctly, did not avoid the noble and powerful, and guests dared not come to his gate; many people harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office he enforced the law with stern rectitude, showed no deference to the nobility, and guests dared not approach his gate; resentment spread widely.

sentences.zh: 士文從父妹為齊氏嬪，有色，齊滅之後，賜薛國公長孫覽為妾。

translations.literal: His father's younger sister's daughter had been a concubine of Qi and was beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue, as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin had been a concubine of Qi and was beautiful; after Qi fell she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue, as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 覽妻鄭氏性妒，譖之於文獻後，後令覽離絕。

translations.literal: Lan's wife Lady Zheng was jealous and slandered her to Empress Dowager Wenxian; the empress had Lan separate from her.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's wife Lady Zheng was jealous and slandered her to Empress Dowager Wenxian, who ordered Lan to dismiss her.

sentences.zh: 士文恥之，不與相見。

translations.literal: Shiwen was shamed by this and would not meet with her.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen was ashamed of this and refused to see her.

sentences.zh: 後應州刺史唐君明居母憂，娉以為妻，由是士文、君明並為禦史所劾。

translations.literal: Later Yingzhou Governor Tang Junming, while in mourning for his mother, took her in marriage; for this Shiwen and Junming were both impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yingzhou Governor Tang Junming, while mourning his mother, took her as wife; for this both Shiwen and Junming were impeached by the censor.

sentences.zh: 士文性剛，在獄數日，憤恚而死。

translations.literal: Shiwen was stern by nature; after several days in prison he died of rage and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen was unyielding by nature; after several days in prison he died of rage.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，有子三人，朝夕不繼，親友無內之者。

translations.literal: His household had no surplus wealth; he had three sons who from morning to evening had nothing to eat, and relatives and friends would not take them in.
translations.idiomatic: His household had no surplus; he left three sons who could not secure their next meal, and neither kin nor friends would shelter them.

sentences.zh: ○田式

translations.literal: ○ Tian Shi
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shi

sentences.zh: 田式，字顯標，馮翊下邦人也。

translations.literal: Tian Shi, style Xianbiao, was a man of Xiabang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shi, courtesy name Xianbiao, was a native of Xiabang in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 祖安興，父長樂，仕魏，俱為本郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Anxing and father Changle both served Wei as governors of their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Anxing and his father Changle both served Wei as governors of their home commandery.

sentences.zh: 式性剛果，多武藝，拳勇絕人。

translations.literal: Shi was firm and resolute by nature, skilled in many martial arts, and peerless in boxing courage.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was firm and resolute, skilled in martial arts, and unmatched in physical prowess.

sentences.zh: 周明帝時，年十八，授都督，領鄉兵。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou, at age eighteen he was appointed Colonel and commanded district troops.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Zhou, at eighteen he was appointed Colonel and commanded local militia.

sentences.zh: 後數載，拜渭南太守，政尚嚴猛，吏人重足而立，無敢違法者。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed Governor of Weinan; his administration favored severity and fierceness, and clerks and people stood with feet together, none daring to violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Governor of Weinan. His rule was severe and fierce; officials and commoners stood with feet together, none daring to break the law.

sentences.zh: 遷本郡太守，親故屏跡，請托不行。

translations.literal: Transferred to governor of his native commandery, relatives and friends withdrew from sight and requests for favor went nowhere.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to governor of his home commandery, kin and friends vanished from sight and no plea for favor could pass.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞而善之，進位儀同三司，賜爵信都縣公，擢拜延州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard and approved, promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xindu County, and selected him as Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of this with approval, promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xindu, and appointed him Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從帝平齊，以功加上開府，徙為建州刺史，改封梁泉縣公。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, for merit he was given Superlative Pillar of State, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for his merit was made Superlative Pillar of State, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan.

sentences.zh: 高祖總百揆，尉迥作亂鄴城，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu assumed overall command, Wei Chong rose in rebellion at Yecheng; he followed Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu assumed overall command, Wei Chong rebelled at Yecheng and Shi followed Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.

sentences.zh: 以功拜大將軍，進爵武山郡公。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Great General and advanced in rank to Duke of Wushan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Great General and advanced to Duke of Wushan.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜襄州總管，專以立威為務。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the abdication he was appointed General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou, devoting himself solely to establishing authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was made General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou and devoted himself solely to imposing his authority.

sentences.zh: 每視事于外，必盛氣以待其下，官屬股栗，無敢仰視。

translations.literal: Whenever he conducted business outside, he must display stern air to await those below; officials trembled and none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he held court outside he displayed a fierce demeanor toward his subordinates; his staff trembled and none dared meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 有犯禁者，雖至親昵，無所容貸。

translations.literal: Whoever violated prohibitions, even close intimates, he would not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever broke his rules, even close kin, received no leniency.

sentences.zh: 其女婿京兆杜甯，自長安省之，式誡寧無出入。

translations.literal: His son-in-law Du Ning of Jingzhao came from Chang'an to visit him; Shi warned Ning not to go out.
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Du Ning of Jingzhao came from Chang'an to visit; Shi forbade Ning to go out.

sentences.zh: 寧久之不得還，竊上北樓，以暢羈思。

translations.literal: Ning long could not return; he secretly went up the north tower to ease his detained thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to leave for a long time, Ning secretly climbed the north tower to ease his longing.

sentences.zh: 式知之，笞寧五十。

translations.literal: When Shi learned of it he flogged Ning fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi learned of this he had Ning beaten fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 其所愛奴，嘗詣式白事，有蟲上其衣衿，揮袖拂去之。

translations.literal: A favorite slave once came to report to Shi; a bug climbed on his collar and he waved his sleeve to brush it off.
translations.idiomatic: A favorite slave once came to report to him; an insect crawled on his collar and the slave brushed it away with his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 式以為慢己，立棒殺之。

translations.literal: Shi considered this disrespect to himself and immediately had him clubbed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shi took this as disrespect and had him beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 或僚吏奸贓，部內劫盜者，無問輕重，悉禁地牢中，寢處糞穢，令其苦毒，自非身死，終不得出。

translations.literal: Whether subordinate officials were corrupt or bandits robbed within the commandery, regardless of severity he shut them all in an underground cell, made them sleep amid filth, and inflicted bitter suffering; unless they died they could never come out.
translations.idiomatic: Whether an official was corrupt or a bandit struck within his territory, regardless of severity he confined them in a dungeon amid filth until they suffered bitterly; unless they died they never emerged.

sentences.zh: 每赦書到州，式未暇讀，先召獄卒，殺重囚，然後宣示百姓。

translations.literal: Whenever an amnesty edict reached the province, before Shi had time to read it he first summoned the jailers to kill the heavy criminals, then proclaimed it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an amnesty reached his province, before reading it he first summoned the jailers to execute the serious criminals, then announced the edict to the people.

sentences.zh: 其刻暴如此。

translations.literal: His severity and cruelty were like this.
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 由是為上所譴，除名為百姓。

translations.literal: For this the emperor reprimanded him and removed his name, making him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: For this the emperor censured him, struck his name from the rolls, and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 式慚恚不食，妻子至其所，輒怒，唯侍僮二人給使左右。

translations.literal: Shi, ashamed and resentful, would not eat; when wife and children came to his place he would rage, and only two attending slaves waited on him left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and furious, Shi refused food; when wife and children came he raged at them, and only two attendant slaves waited on him.

sentences.zh: 從家中索椒，欲以自殺，家人不與。

translations.literal: He asked his household for pepper, intending to kill himself; his family would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his household for pepper to kill himself, but his family refused.

sentences.zh: 陰遣所侍僮詣市買毒藥，妻子又奪而棄之。

translations.literal: He secretly sent his attendant slaves to the market to buy poison; his wife and children again seized and discarded it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent his slaves to buy poison at market, but his wife seized and discarded it.

sentences.zh: 式恚臥。

translations.literal: Shi lay abed in rage.
translations.idiomatic: Shi lay abed in fury.

sentences.zh: 其子信時為儀同，至式前流涕曰：「大人既是朝廷舊臣，又無大過。

translations.literal: His son Xin was then a Grand Master for Court Audience; he came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are both an old minister of the court and have committed no great fault.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin, then a court grandee, came weeping and said, "Father, you are a veteran minister of the court and have committed no grave offense.

sentences.zh: 比見公卿放辱者多矣，旋複升用，大人何能久乎？

translations.literal: Recently I have seen many dukes and ministers publicly humiliated who soon rose again—how can Father endure this long?
translations.idiomatic: I have lately seen many nobles publicly shamed who were soon restored—how can you bear to remain in this state?

sentences.zh: 乃至於此！」

translations.literal: To come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: How did it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 式欻然而起，抽刀斫信，信遽走避之，刃中於閾。

translations.literal: Shi suddenly rose, drew a knife, and hacked at Xin; Xin hastily fled to avoid it, and the blade struck the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: Shi suddenly rose, drew a knife, and hacked at Xin; Xin fled in haste and the blade struck the door sill.

sentences.zh: 上知之，以式為罪己之深，複其官爵。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and, considering that Shi's guilt toward himself was deep, restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this and, judging that Shi's self-reproach ran deep, restored his office and rank.

sentences.zh: 尋拜廣州總管，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: ○燕榮

translations.literal: ○ Yan Rong
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rong

sentences.zh: 燕榮，字貴公，華陰弘農人也。

translations.literal: Yan Rong, style Guigong, was a man of Hongnong in Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rong, courtesy name Guigong, was a native of Hongnong in Huayin.

sentences.zh: 父偘，周大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Kan was a Great General of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan was a Great General of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 榮性剛嚴，有武藝，仕周為內侍上士。

translations.literal: Rong was firm and stern by nature, possessed martial arts, and under Zhou served as Superior Attendant of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was stern and martial by nature and under Zhou served as Superior Attendant of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 從武帝伐齊，以功授開府儀同三司，封高邑縣公。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in attacking Qi, for merit he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment and enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the campaign against Qi and for merit was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment and enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進位大將軍，封落叢郡公，拜晉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was advanced to Great General, enfeoffed as Duke of Luocong Commandery, and appointed Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was promoted to Great General, enfeoffed as Duke of Luocong, and appointed Governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從河間王弘擊突厥，以功拜上柱國，遷青州總管。

translations.literal: Following Prince of Hejian Hong in attacking the Turks, for merit he was appointed Pillar of State and transferred to General-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served under the Prince of Hejian in the attack on the Turks, and for merit was made Pillar of State and transferred to General-in-Chief of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮在州，選絕有力者為伍伯，吏人過之者，必加詰問，輒楚撻之，創多見骨。

translations.literal: Rong in his province selected the strongest men as ward chiefs; whoever passed among clerks and people he invariably interrogated and then flogged with the cudgel, wounds often showing bone.
translations.idiomatic: At his province Rong selected the strongest men as ward chiefs; whenever officials or commoners passed by they were questioned and beaten with the cudgel until wounds often exposed the bone.

sentences.zh: 奸盜屏跡，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Wickedness and banditry vanished from sight; within the borders all was solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits vanished and the realm within his borders grew solemn and orderly.

sentences.zh: 他州縣人行經其界者，畏若寇仇，不敢休息。

translations.literal: People from other prefectures and counties who traveled through his borders feared him as bandit enemies and dared not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers from other jurisdictions who passed through his territory feared him as they would bandits and dared not pause to rest.

sentences.zh: 上甚善之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved of him.

sentences.zh: 後因入朝覲，特加勞勉。

translations.literal: Later when he entered court for an audience he was specially given consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he came to court for an audience, the emperor personally commended and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 榮以母老，請每歲入朝，上許之。

translations.literal: Rong, because his mother was old, requested to enter court each year; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly, Rong asked to attend court every year, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 及辭，上賜宴於內殿，詔王公作詩以餞之。

translations.literal: When he took leave, the emperor gave a banquet in the inner hall and ordered dukes and princes to compose poems to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell the emperor hosted a banquet in the inner palace and ordered the nobles to compose parting poems.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，以為行軍總管，率水軍自東萊傍海，入太湖，取吳郡。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he was made Campaign Commander, leading the naval army from Donglai along the sea into Tai Lake to take Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he served as Campaign Commander, leading a naval force from Donglai along the coast into Lake Tai to seize Wujun.

sentences.zh: 既破丹陽，吳人共立蕭瓛為主，阻兵于晉陵，為宇文述所敗，退保包山。

translations.literal: After Danyang was broken, the people of Wu together set up Xiao Huan as leader, blocked the army at Jinling, were defeated by Yuwen Shu, and retreated to hold Baoshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Danyang fell, the people of Wu set up Xiao Huan as their leader, resisted at Jinling, were defeated by Yuwen Shu, and withdrew to hold Baoshan.

sentences.zh: 榮率精甲五千躡之，瓛敗走，為榮所執，晉陵、會稽悉平。

translations.literal: Rong led five thousand elite armored troops in pursuit; Huan was defeated and fled, was seized by Rong, and Jinling and Kuaiji were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rong pursued with five thousand elite troops; Huan was defeated, captured by Rong, and Jinling and Kuaiji were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 檢校揚州總管。

translations.literal: He was made Acting General-in-Chief of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting General-in-Chief of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋征為右武候將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to serve as General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇邊，以為行軍總管，屯幽州。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the border he was made Campaign Commander and garrisoned Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier he was made Campaign Commander and stationed at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 明年，起為幽州總管。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled as General-in-Chief of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as General-in-Chief of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮性嚴酷，有威容，長史見者，莫不惶懼自失。

translations.literal: Rong was stern and cruel by nature, with a formidable presence; when the Chief Clerk saw him none failed to lose themselves in dread.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Rong was stern and cruel, with a formidable bearing; chief clerks who met him invariably lost their composure in fear.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧氏，代為著姓，榮皆署為吏卒以屈辱之。

translations.literal: The Lu clan of Fanyang had for generations been a prominent surname; Rong all appointed them as clerks and runners to humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu clan of Fanyang had long been a prominent lineage; Rong appointed them all as lowly clerks and runners to humiliate them.

sentences.zh: 鞭笞左右，動至千數，流血盈前，飲啖自若。

translations.literal: He flogged those at his side, often reaching a thousand strokes; blood filled the ground before him, yet he ate and drank as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He beat those around him, often to a thousand strokes; blood pooled before him while he ate and drank as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 嘗按部，道次見叢荊，堪為笞棰，命取之，輒以試人。

translations.literal: Once on an inspection tour he saw a thicket of brambles along the road suitable for cudgels, ordered them taken, and always used them to test people.
translations.idiomatic: Once on tour he saw brambles along the road fit for cudgels, had them gathered, and used them to test people.

sentences.zh: 人或自陳無咎，榮曰：「後若有罪，當免爾。」

translations.literal: If someone declared himself guiltless, Rong said: "If later you have guilt, you shall be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: If someone protested innocence, Rong said, "If you commit an offense later, I shall pardon you for this."

sentences.zh: 及後犯細過，將撾之，人曰：「前日被杖，使君許有罪宥之。」

translations.literal: Later when they committed a minor fault and he was about to beat them, the person said: "The other day I was beaten and the lord promised that if guilty I would be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Later when they committed a minor offense and he was about to beat them, the man said, "The other day you beat me and promised to pardon any later offense."

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「無過尚爾，況有過邪！」

translations.literal: Rong said: "When there was no fault it was still thus—how much more when there is fault!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "When you were guiltless I still beat you—how much more when you are guilty!"

sentences.zh: 榜棰如舊。

translations.literal: The cudgel blows were as before.
translations.idiomatic: The beating proceeded as before.

sentences.zh: 榮每巡省管內，聞官人及百姓妻女有美色，輒舍其室而淫之。

translations.literal: Whenever Rong toured within his jurisdiction, if he heard that an official or commoner had a beautiful wife or daughter he would occupy their house and violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Rong toured his territory and heard that an official or commoner had a beautiful wife or daughter, he would take over their house and violate her.

sentences.zh: 貪暴放縱日甚。

translations.literal: Greed, cruelty, and indulgence grew daily worse.
translations.idiomatic: His greed, cruelty, and license grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 是時元弘嗣被除為幽州長史，懼為榮所辱，固辭。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Hongsi was removed and appointed Chief Administrator of Youzhou; he feared being humiliated by Rong and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Hongsi was appointed Chief Administrator of Youzhou and, fearing humiliation by Rong, firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上知之，敕榮曰：「弘嗣杖十已上罪，皆須奏聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and ordered Rong: "For Hongsi, any offense warranting ten strokes or more must be reported."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this and instructed Rong, "Any offense by Hongsi warranting ten strokes or more must be reported to the throne."

sentences.zh: 榮忿曰：「豎子何敢弄我！」

translations.literal: Rong said in anger: "How dare that stripling toy with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong raged, "How dare that stripling play games with me!"

sentences.zh: 於是遣弘嗣監納倉粟，颺得一糠一秕，輒罰之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Hongsi to supervise the intake of granary grain; if a single husk or chaff was winnowed out he would punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Hongsi to supervise granary intake; for every husk or chaff winnowed out he imposed punishment.

sentences.zh: 每笞雖不滿十，然一日之中，或至三數。

translations.literal: Though each beating did not reach ten strokes, in a single day there might be two or three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Though each beating fell short of ten strokes, in a single day there might be two or three rounds.

sentences.zh: 如是歷年，怨隙日構，榮遂收付獄，禁絕其糧。

translations.literal: Thus for years grievance and rancor built daily; Rong then had him seized and put in prison and cut off his food.
translations.idiomatic: For years resentment mounted; Rong then had him imprisoned and cut off his provisions.

sentences.zh: 弘嗣饑餒，抽衣絮，雜水咽之。

translations.literal: Hongsi, starving, tore cloth padding and swallowed it mixed with water.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, Hongsi tore padding from his clothes and swallowed it with water.

sentences.zh: 其妻詣闕稱冤，上遣考功侍郎劉士龍馳驛鞫問。

translations.literal: His wife went to the palace to plead injustice; the emperor sent Reviewing Officer Liu Shilong post-haste by relay to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: His wife appealed at court; the emperor sent Reviewing Officer Liu Shilong by urgent relay to investigate.

sentences.zh: 奏榮虐毒非虛，又賊穢狼籍，遂征還京師，賜死。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Rong's cruelty was not false, and that theft and defilement were everywhere; Rong was then summoned back to the capital and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reported that Rong's cruelty was real and that plunder and defilement were rampant; Rong was summoned to the capital and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 先是，榮家寢室無故有蛆數斛，從地墳出。

translations.literal: Before this, in Rong's sleeping quarters maggots suddenly appeared by the bushel, burrowing up from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, maggots suddenly appeared by the bushel in Rong's bedchamber, burrowing up from the ground.

sentences.zh: 未幾，榮死於蛆出之處。

translations.literal: Before long Rong died at the place where the maggots had emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Rong died at the very spot where the maggots had appeared.

sentences.zh: 有子詢。

translations.literal: He had a son Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Xun.

sentences.zh: ○趙仲卿

translations.literal: ○ Zhao Zhongqing
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhongqing

sentences.zh: 趙仲卿，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhongqing was a man of Longxi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhongqing was a native of Longxi in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父剛，周大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Gang was a Great General of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gang was a Great General of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仲卿性粗暴，有膂力，周齊王憲甚禮之。

translations.literal: Zhongqing was rough and violent by nature, possessed great physical strength, and Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing was rough and violent, possessed great strength, and Prince Xian of Qi treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 從擊齊，攻臨秦、統戎、威遠、伏龍、張壁等五城，盡平之。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Qi he assaulted the five cities of Linqin, Tongrong, Weiyuan, Fulong, and Zhangbi, and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Qi he attacked the five cities of Linqin, Tongrong, Weiyuan, Fulong, and Zhangbi and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 又擊齊將段孝先于姚襄城，苦戰連日，破之。

translations.literal: He also attacked Qi general Duan Xiaoxian at Yaoxiang Fortress; after bitter fighting for many days he broke him.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the Qi general Duan Xiaoxian at Yaoxiang; after days of bitter fighting he defeated him.

sentences.zh: 以功授大都督，尋典宿衛。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Great Colonel and soon managed palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was appointed Great Colonel and soon managed palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，以功遷上儀同，兼趙郡太守。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi, for merit he was transferred to Senior Grand Master for Court Audience and concurrently Magistrate of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the pacification of Qi he was promoted to Senior Grand Master for Court Audience and concurrently made Magistrate of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為畿伯中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered service as Metropolitan Commandery Central Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Metropolitan Commandery Central Grandee.

sentences.zh: 王謙作亂，仲卿使在利州，即與總管豆盧勣發兵拒守。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled, Zhongqing was on mission in Lizhou; he immediately joined the General-in-Chief Dou Lu Ji in raising troops to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Zhongqing was in Lizhou and at once joined General-in-Chief Dou Lu Ji in raising troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 為謙所攻，仲卿督兵出戰，前後一十七陣。

translations.literal: Attacked by Qian, Zhongqing supervised troops in going out to battle, seventeen formations in all before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged by Qian, Zhongqing led troops into battle in seventeen engagements.

sentences.zh: 及謙平，進位大將軍，封長垣縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Qian was pacified he was advanced to Great General, enfeoffed as Duke of Changyuan County with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian was suppressed he was promoted to Great General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changyuan with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵河北郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication his rank was advanced to Duke of Hebei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne his rank was advanced to Duke of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 開皇三年，突厥犯塞，以行軍總管從河間王弘出賀蘭山。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; as Campaign Commander he followed the Prince of Hejian Hong out to Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaihuang, when the Turks raided the frontier, he served as Campaign Commander under the Prince of Hejian to Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 仲卿別道俱進，無虜而還。

translations.literal: Zhongqing took a separate route and advanced together, found no barbarians, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing advanced by a separate route, found no enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 複鎮平涼，尋拜石州刺史。

translations.literal: He again garrisoned Pingliang and soon was appointed Governor of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again garrisoned Pingliang and was soon appointed Governor of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 法令嚴猛，纖微之失，無所容舍，鞭笞長史，輒至二百。

translations.literal: Laws and ordinances were stern and fierce; the slightest fault found no tolerance, and he flogged the Chief Clerk up to two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were stern and fierce; the slightest fault received no leniency, and he flogged the Chief Clerk up to two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 官人戰慄，無敢違犯，盜賊屏息，皆稱其能。

translations.literal: Officials trembled with fear and none dared violate; bandits were silenced, and all praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Officials trembled with fear and none dared offend; bandits were silenced, and all praised his effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 遷兗州刺史，未之官，拜朔州總管。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Yanzhou, before taking office he was appointed General-in-Chief of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Yanzhou but, before taking office, was appointed General-in-Chief of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 于時塞北盛興屯田，仲卿總管統之。

translations.literal: At that time garrison farming flourished north of the frontier; Zhongqing had overall command of it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military colonies flourished on the northern frontier, and Zhongqing had overall command.

sentences.zh: 微有不理者，仲卿輒召主掌，撻其胸背，或解衣倒曳於荊棘中。

translations.literal: For the slightest irregularity Zhongqing would summon the person in charge and beat his chest and back, or strip him and drag him backward through brambles.
translations.idiomatic: For the slightest irregularity he summoned the responsible officer, beat his chest and back, or stripped him and dragged him through brambles.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之猛獸。

translations.literal: People of the time called him a fierce beast.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day called him a savage beast.

sentences.zh: 事多克濟，由是收穫歲廣，邊戍無饋運之憂。

translations.literal: Matters mostly succeeded; because of this harvests grew yearly broader and frontier garrisons had no worry of supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: His methods mostly succeeded; harvests grew year by year and frontier garrisons no longer feared supply shortages.

sentences.zh: 會突厥啟民可汗求婚于國，上許之。

translations.literal: It happened that Qimin Khan of the Turks sought marriage with the state; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qimin Khan of the Turks sought a marriage alliance; the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 仲卿因是間其骨肉，遂相攻擊。

translations.literal: Zhongqing took advantage of this to sow discord among their kin, and they thereupon attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing exploited this to sow discord among their kin, and they soon attacked one another.

sentences.zh: 十七年，啟民窘迫，與隋使長孫晟投通漢鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Qimin was hard pressed and, with Sui envoy Changsun Sheng, fled to seek refuge at Han Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Qimin, hard pressed, fled with Sui envoy Changsun Sheng to seek refuge at Han Fort.

sentences.zh: 仲卿率騎千餘馳援之，達頭不敢逼。

translations.literal: Zhongqing led more than a thousand horsemen in rapid relief; Tardu dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing rode with more than a thousand cavalry to relieve him; Tardu dared not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 潛遣人誘致啟民所部，至者二萬餘家。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent men to lure Qimin's tribes; more than twenty thousand households came.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent men to lure Qimin's tribes, and more than twenty thousand households came over.

sentences.zh: 其年，從高熲指白道以擊達頭。

translations.literal: That year he followed Gao Jiong in pointing toward the White Road to strike Tardu.
translations.idiomatic: That year he followed Gao Jiong along the White Road to strike Tardu.

sentences.zh: 仲卿率兵三千為前鋒，至族蠡山，與虜相遇，交戰七日，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhongqing led three thousand troops as vanguard; reaching Zulü Mountain he met the barbarians and fought seven days, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing led three thousand men as vanguard; at Zulü Mountain he met the enemy and after seven days of fighting won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 追奔至乞伏泊，複破之，虜千餘口，雜畜萬計。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout to Qifu Marsh he again defeated them, taking more than a thousand captives and livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Qifu Marsh he defeated them again, taking more than a thousand captives and tens of thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 突厥悉眾而至，仲卿為方陣，四面拒戰。

translations.literal: The Turks came with their full host; Zhongqing formed a square battle array and resisted on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks came in full force; Zhongqing formed a square array and fought on four sides.

sentences.zh: 經五日，會高熲大兵至，合擊之，虜乃敗走。

translations.literal: After five days Gao Jiong's great army arrived; joining in attack the barbarians then fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: After five days Gao Jiong's main force arrived; joining battle they drove the enemy to flight.

sentences.zh: 追度白道，逾秦山七百餘裡。

translations.literal: In pursuit they crossed the White Road and went beyond Qin Mountain for more than seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit crossed the White Road and went more than seven hundred li beyond Qin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時突厥降者萬餘家，上命仲卿處之恆安。

translations.literal: At that time more than ten thousand Turk households had surrendered; the emperor ordered Zhongqing to settle them at Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than ten thousand Turk households had surrendered; the emperor ordered Zhongqing to settle them at Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 以功進位上柱國，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Pillar of State and granted three thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was advanced to Pillar of State and granted three thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮達頭掩襲啟民，令仲卿屯兵二萬以備之，代州總管韓洪、永康公李藥王、蔚州刺史劉隆等，將步騎一萬鎮恆安。

translations.literal: The court feared Tardu would launch a surprise attack on Qimin and ordered Zhongqing to garrison twenty thousand troops in readiness; Acting General-in-Chief of Daizhou Han Hong, Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, and Governor of Wei Zhou Liu Long and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared Tardu would strike Qimin by surprise and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in reserve; Han Hong, Acting General-in-Chief of Daizhou, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, Governor of Wei, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 達頭騎十萬來寇，韓洪軍大敗，仲卿自樂寧鎮邀擊，斬首虜千餘級。

translations.literal: Tardu came raiding with a hundred thousand horsemen; Han Hong's army was greatly defeated; Zhongqing from Lening Fort intercepted and beheaded more than a thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Tardu raided with a hundred thousand horsemen; Han Hong's army was routed; Zhongqing intercepted from Lening Fort and beheaded more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 明年，督役築金河、定襄二城，以居啟民。

translations.literal: The next year he supervised labor in building the Jinhe and Dingxiang forts to house Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he supervised construction of the Jinhe and Dingxiang forts to house Qimin.

sentences.zh: 時有表言仲卿酷暴者，上令禦史王偉按之，並實，惜其功不罪也。

translations.literal: At that time there were memorials saying Zhongqing was cruel and violent; the emperor ordered Censor Wang Wei to investigate—all proved true, yet cherishing his merit he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials then accused Zhongqing of cruelty; the emperor ordered Censor Wang Wei to investigate—all proved true, yet valuing his merit he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 因勞之曰：「知公清正，為下所惡。」

translations.literal: He thereupon consoled him, saying: "I know you are upright and pure, and are hated by those below."
translations.idiomatic: He then comforted him, saying, "I know you are upright and pure, and are hated by your subordinates."

sentences.zh: 賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He granted five hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him five hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 仲卿益恣，由是免官。

translations.literal: Zhongqing grew still more unrestrained, and for this was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing grew still more unrestrained and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，檢校司農卿。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was made Acting Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign he served as Acting Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之得罪，奉詔往益州窮按之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shu Xiu fell into guilt he was ordered by edict to go to Yizhou and investigate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu Xiu fell from grace he was ordered to Yizhou to investigate exhaustively.

sentences.zh: 秀賓客經過之處，仲卿必深文致法，州縣長吏坐者太半。

translations.literal: Wherever Xiu's guests had passed, Zhongqing invariably twisted the law to the utmost; prefectural and county chief administrators implicated numbered more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Xiu's associates had passed, Zhongqing twisted the law to ensnare them; more than half the prefectural and county chiefs were implicated.

sentences.zh: 上以為能，賞婢奴五十口，黃金二百兩，米粟五千石，奇寶雜物稱是。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him capable and rewarded fifty slave women and men, two hundred taels of gold, five thousand shi of grain, and rare treasures and miscellaneous goods in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him capable and rewarded him with fifty slave men and women, two hundred taels of gold, five thousand shi of grain, and rare treasures in like measure.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，判兵部、工部二曹尚書事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he concurrently judged the two ministries of War and Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he concurrently oversaw the ministries of War and Works.

sentences.zh: 其年，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Solemn.

sentences.zh: 贈物五百段。

translations.literal: Five hundred lengths of goods were granted in gift.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred lengths of goods were granted in burial gifts.

sentences.zh: 子弘嗣。

translations.literal: His son was Hongsi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hongsi.

sentences.zh: 崔弘度弟弘升

translations.literal: Cui Hongdu and his younger brother Hongsheng
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongdu and his younger brother Hongsheng

sentences.zh: 崔弘度，字摩訶衍，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Hongdu, style Moheyan, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongdu, courtesy name Moheyan, was a native of Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖楷，魏司空。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai was Minister of Works of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai was Minister of Works of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父說，周敷州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yue was Governor of Fuzhou in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue was Governor of Fuzhou under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 弘度膂力絕人，儀貌魁岸，須面甚偉。

translations.literal: Hongdu's physical strength was peerless; his bearing was towering, and his beard and face were very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu possessed peerless strength; his stature was towering and his beard and face remarkably imposing.

sentences.zh: 性嚴酷。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was stern and cruel.

sentences.zh: 年十七，周大塚宰宇文護引為親信。

translations.literal: At age seventeen Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu of Zhou brought him in as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu of Zhou took him as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督，累轉大都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Colonel and repeatedly transferred to Great Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Colonel and repeatedly promoted to Great Colonel.

sentences.zh: 時護子中山公訓為蒲州刺史，令弘度從焉。

translations.literal: At that time Hu's son the Duke of Zhongshan Xun was Governor of Pu Prefecture, and he ordered Hongdu to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hu's son, the Duke of Zhongshan Xun, was Governor of Pu Prefecture, and Hongdu accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與訓登樓，至上層，去地四五丈，俯臨之，訓曰：「可畏也。」

translations.literal: Once he climbed a tower with Xun to the upper story, four or five zhang above the ground; looking down Xun said: "It is fearful."
translations.idiomatic: Once he climbed with Xun to the upper story, four or five zhang above the ground; looking down Xun said, "How frightening."

sentences.zh: 弘度曰：「此何足畏！」

translations.literal: Hongdu said: "This is nothing to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu said, "This is nothing to fear!"

sentences.zh: 欻然擲下，至地無損傷。

translations.literal: Suddenly he threw himself down and reached the ground without injury.
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly leapt down and reached the ground unharmed.

sentences.zh: 訓以其拳捷，大奇之。

translations.literal: Xun, because of his nimble fists, greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was astonished by his swift fists.

sentences.zh: 後以戰勳，授儀同。

translations.literal: Later for battle merit he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: For battle merit he was later appointed Grand Master for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 從武帝滅齊，進位上開府，鄴縣公，賜物三千段，粟麥三千石，奴婢百口，雜畜千計。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in destroying Qi he was advanced to Superlative Pillar of State, Duke of Ye County, granted three thousand lengths of goods, three thousand shi of grain and millet, a hundred slave men and women, and livestock by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu conquered Qi he was promoted to Superlative Pillar of State and Duke of Ye, granted three thousand lengths of goods, three thousand shi of grain, a hundred slaves, and thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 尋從汝南公宇文神舉破盧昌期於范陽。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the Duke of Runan Yuwen Shenju in breaking Lu Changqi at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the Duke of Runan Yuwen Shenju in defeating Lu Changqi at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，從鄖國公韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he followed the Duke of Yun Guo Wei Xiaokuan in planning the Huainan region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he followed the Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan in operations along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 弘度與化政公宇文忻、司水賀婁子幹至肥口，陳將潘琛率兵數千來拒戰，隔水而陣。

translations.literal: Hongdu with the Duke of Transformational Governance Yuwen Xin and Director of Waters Helou Zigan reached Feikou; Chen general Pan Chen led several thousand troops to resist battle and arrayed across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu, with the Duke of Transformational Governance Yuwen Xin and Director of Waters Helou Zigan, reached Feikou; the Chen general Pan Chen led several thousand men to resist and arrayed across the water.

sentences.zh: 忻遣弘度諭以禍福，琛至夕而遁。

translations.literal: Xin sent Hongdu to instruct him on fortune and calamity; Chen fled by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Xin sent Hongdu to admonish him with warnings of fortune and ruin; Chen withdrew by evening.

sentences.zh: 進攻壽陽，降陳守將吳文立，弘度功最。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Shouyang, the Chen defender Wu Wenli surrendered; Hongdu's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Shouyang the Chen defender Wu Wenli surrendered; Hongdu's merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 以前後勳，進位上大將軍，襲父爵安平縣公。

translations.literal: For former and later merit he was advanced to Senior Great General and inherited his father's enfeoffment as Duke of Anping County.
translations.idiomatic: For cumulative merit he was promoted to Senior Great General and inherited his father's title as Duke of Anping.

sentences.zh: 及尉迥作亂，以弘度為行軍總管，從韋孝寬討之。

translations.literal: When Wei Chong rebelled, Hongdu was made Campaign Commander and followed Wei Xiaokuan to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chong rebelled, Hongdu served as Campaign Commander under Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 弘度募長安驍雄數百人為別隊，所當無不披靡。

translations.literal: Hongdu recruited several hundred fierce champions of Chang'an as a separate corps; wherever they faced none failed to scatter the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu recruited several hundred of Chang'an's fiercest fighters as a separate corps; wherever they struck the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 弘度妹先適迥子為妻，及破鄴城，迥窘迫升樓，弘度直上龍尾追之。

translations.literal: Hongdu's younger sister had earlier been given in marriage to Chong's son as wife; when Yecheng was broken Chong, hard pressed, ascended a tower, and Hongdu climbed straight up the Dragon Tail ramp in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu's sister had married Chong's son; when Yecheng fell Chong fled up a tower in distress, and Hongdu climbed the Dragon Tail ramp in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 迥彎弓將射弘度，弘度脫兜鍪謂迥曰：「相識不？

translations.literal: Chong bent his bow intending to shoot Hongdu; Hongdu removed his helmet and said to Chong: "Do you recognize me?
translations.idiomatic: Chong drew his bow to shoot Hongdu; Hongdu removed his helmet and said, "Do you know who I am?

sentences.zh: 今日各圖國事，不得顧私。

translations.literal: Today each plots for the state's affairs and cannot attend to private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Today we each serve the state and cannot indulge private ties.

sentences.zh: 以親戚之情，謹遏亂兵，不許侵辱。

translations.literal: Out of kinship I strictly restrain the disorderly troops and do not permit insult and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Out of kinship I have restrained the troops from insult and abuse.

sentences.zh: 事勢如此，早為身計，何所待也？」

translations.literal: The situation is thus—make early provision for yourself; what are you waiting for?"
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand as they do—look to your own safety. What are you waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 迥擲弓於地，罵大丞相極口而自殺。

translations.literal: Chong cast his bow to the ground, cursed the Grand Chancellor to the utmost, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chong threw down his bow, cursed the Grand Chancellor bitterly, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 弘度顧其弟弘升曰：「汝可取迥頭。」

translations.literal: Hongdu turned to his younger brother Hongsheng and said: "You may take Chong's head."
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu told his brother Hongsheng, "Take Chong's head."

sentences.zh: 弘升遂斬之，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: Hongsheng thereupon beheaded him; Hongdu was advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsheng beheaded him, and Hongdu was advanced to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 時行軍總管例封國公，弘度不時殺迥，致縱惡言，由是降爵一等，為武鄉郡公。

translations.literal: At that time Campaign Commanders were by rule enfeoffed as dukes of a state; because Hongdu did not kill Chong in time, allowing slander to spread, for this his rank was lowered one grade to Duke of Wuxiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign commanders were normally enfeoffed as state dukes, but because Hongdu had not killed Chong promptly and allowed slander to spread, his rank was reduced one grade to Duke of Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，突厥入寇，弘度以行軍總管出原州以拒之。

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang the Turks invaded; Hongdu as Campaign Commander went out from Yuanzhou to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaihuang, when the Turks invaded, Hongdu marched from Yuanzhou as Campaign Commander to resist them.

sentences.zh: 虜退，弘度進屯靈武。

translations.literal: The barbarians retreated and Hongdu advanced to garrison Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew and Hongdu advanced to garrison Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 月余而還，拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a month he returned and was appointed Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he returned and was appointed Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 納其妹為秦孝王妃。

translations.literal: He gave his younger sister in marriage to the Prince of Qin as consort.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his younger sister in marriage to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 尋遷襄州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘度素貴，禦下嚴急，動行捶罰，吏人讋氣，聞其聲，莫不戰慄。

translations.literal: Hongdu had always been noble; in governing subordinates he was stern and urgent, always applying beatings and punishments; clerks and people were cowed by his spirit, and at his sound none failed to tremble with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu had always been high-born; he governed subordinates with stern urgency, beating and punishing at every turn; officials and commoners trembled at the sound of his name.

sentences.zh: 所在之處，令行禁止，盜賊屏跡。

translations.literal: Wherever he was, orders were executed and prohibitions observed; bandits vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, his orders were obeyed and bandits vanished.

sentences.zh: 梁王蕭琮來朝，上以弘度為江陵總管，鎮荊州。

translations.literal: When Liang Prince Xiao Cong came to court the emperor made Hongdu General-in-Chief of Jiangling to garrison Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang prince Xiao Cong came to court, the emperor appointed Hongdu General-in-Chief of Jiangling to garrison Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘度未至，而琮叔父嚴擁居人以叛，弘度追之不及。

translations.literal: Before Hongdu arrived, Cong's uncle Yan seized the people in rebellion; Hongdu pursued but could not overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hongdu arrived, Cong's uncle Yan seized the populace in rebellion; Hongdu pursued but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 陳人憚弘度，亦不敢窺荊州。

translations.literal: The Chen people feared Hongdu and also dared not spy on Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen feared Hongdu and dared not probe Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管從秦孝王出襄陽道。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen he was Campaign Commander following the Prince of Qin out by the Xiangyang route.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he served as Campaign Commander under the Prince of Qin along the Xiangyang route.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，賜物五千段。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified he was granted five thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he was granted five thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等作亂，複以行軍總管出泉門道，隸于楊素。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled he again was Campaign Commander out by the Quanmen route, subordinate to Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled he again served as Campaign Commander on the Quanmen route under Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 弘度與素，品同而年長，素每屈下之，一旦隸素，意甚不平，素言多不用。

translations.literal: Hongdu and Su were equal in rank but Hongdu was older; Su always humbled himself before him. Once subordinate to Su, his heart was very unbalanced, and Su's words were mostly not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu and Su were peers, but Hongdu was older and Su always deferred to him. Once placed under Su's command he resented it deeply and mostly ignored Su's orders.

sentences.zh: 素亦優容之。

translations.literal: Su also treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Su nevertheless treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 及還，檢校原州事，仍領行軍總管以備胡，無虜而還，上甚禮之，複以其弟弘升女為河南王妃。

translations.literal: Upon return he was made Acting Governor of Yuanzhou affairs, still holding Campaign Commander to guard against the barbarians; finding no enemy he returned, and the emperor treated him with great courtesy, again giving Hongsheng's daughter in marriage to the Prince of Henan as consort.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he acted as Governor of Yuanzhou and still held command against the barbarians; finding no enemy he returned. The emperor honored him greatly and again gave Hongsheng's daughter to the Prince of Henan as consort.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，檢校太府卿。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was made Acting Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou he served as Acting Minister of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 自以一門二妃，無所降下，每誡其僚吏曰：「人當誠恕，無得欺誑。」

translations.literal: Considering that his house had produced two imperial consorts, he would not humble himself to anyone; he often admonished his subordinate officials: "People should be sincere and forgiving and must not deceive."
translations.idiomatic: With two imperial consorts in his family he bowed to no one; he often warned his staff, "One must be sincere and forbearing and must not deceive."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: All said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 後嘗食鱉，侍者八九人，弘度一一問之曰：「鱉美乎？」

translations.literal: Later when eating turtle he had eight or nine attendants; Hongdu questioned each one: "Is turtle delicious?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, while eating turtle with eight or nine attendants, he asked each, "Is turtle delicious?"

sentences.zh: 人懼之，皆雲：「鱉美。」

translations.literal: People feared him and all said: "Turtle is delicious."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, they all said, "It is delicious."

sentences.zh: 弘度大罵曰：「傭奴何敢誑我？

translations.literal: Hongdu cursed greatly: "Hired slaves—how dare you deceive me!
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu raged, "Servile wretches—how dare you deceive me!

sentences.zh: 汝初未食鱉，安知其美？」

translations.literal: You have not yet eaten turtle—how do you know it is delicious?"
translations.idiomatic: You have never eaten turtle—how would you know it is delicious?"

sentences.zh: 俱杖八十。

translations.literal: All were beaten eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all beaten eighty strokes.

sentences.zh: 官屬百工見之者，莫不流汗，無敢欺隱。

translations.literal: Officials and artisans who saw it all sweated; none dared conceal anything.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and artisans who witnessed it broke into a sweat; none dared conceal anything.

sentences.zh: 時有屈突蓋為武候驃騎，亦嚴刻，長安為之語 曰：「寧飲三升酢，不見崔弘度。

translations.literal: At that time Qu Tu Gai was Rapid Tiger Cavalry General of the Martial Guard, also stern; Chang'an made a saying: "Better drink three sheng of vinegar than see Cui Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Gai of the Martial Guard was likewise severe, and Chang'an said, "Better drink three sheng of vinegar than meet Cui Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 甯茹三升艾，不逢屈突蓋。」

translations.literal: Better endure three sheng of moxa than encounter Qu Tu Gai."
translations.idiomatic: Better endure three sheng of moxa than encounter Qu Tu Gai."

sentences.zh: 然弘度理家如官，子弟斑白，動行捶楚，閨門整肅，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Yet Hongdu managed his household like an office; his sons and younger brothers, though gray-haired, were beaten and flogged when they moved; the inner gates were stern and orderly, and he was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hongdu ran his household like a government office; even gray-haired sons and brothers were beaten for the slightest fault, and his household discipline was praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 未幾，秦王妃以罪誅，河南王妃複被廢黜。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Qin's consort was executed for crime, and the Prince of Henan's consort was again deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Qin's consort was executed for crime and the Prince of Henan's consort was deposed.

sentences.zh: 弘度憂恚，謝病于家，諸弟乃與之別居，彌不得志。

translations.literal: Hongdu, grieved and resentful, pleaded illness at home; his younger brothers then separated to live apart, and he grew still more frustrated.
translations.idiomatic: Grieved and resentful, Hongdu retired ill at home; his brothers moved out to live separately, and his frustration deepened.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，河南王為太子，帝將複立崔妃，遣中使就第宣旨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, the Prince of Henan became heir apparent; the emperor was about to restore Lady Cui as consort and sent a palace envoy to his residence to proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, the Prince of Henan became heir; the emperor intended to restore the Cui consort and sent a palace envoy to proclaim the edict.

sentences.zh: 使者詣弘升家，弘度不之知也。

translations.literal: The envoy went to Hongsheng's house; Hongdu did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy went to Hongsheng's house, and Hongdu knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 使者返，帝曰：「弘度有何言？」

translations.literal: The envoy returned; the emperor said: "What did Hongdu say?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned and the emperor asked, "What did Hongdu say?"

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「弘度稱有疾不起。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Hongdu said he was ill and would not rise."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "Hongdu claimed illness and would not rise."

sentences.zh: 帝默然，其事竟寢。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent, and the matter in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 弘度憂憤，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Hongdu, grieved and indignant, before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Grieved and indignant, Hongdu soon died.

sentences.zh: 弘升字上客，在周為右侍上士。

translations.literal: Hongsheng, styled Shangke, served under Zhou as Attendant Gentleman of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsheng, styled Shangke, served under Zhou as Attendant Gentleman of the Right.

sentences.zh: 尉迥作亂相州，與兄弘度擊之，以功拜上儀同。

translations.literal: When Wei Chong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 尋加上開府，封黃台縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵為公，授驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Hongsheng's rank was advanced to duke and he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Hongsheng's rank was advanced to duke and he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宿衛十餘年，以勳舊遷慈州刺史。

translations.literal: He guarded the palace for more than ten years; as an old meritorious official he was transferred to Governor of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He guarded the palace for more than ten years; as an old meritorious official he was transferred to Governor of Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數歲，轉鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Governor of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to Governor of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後以戚屬之故，待遇愈隆，遷襄州總管。

translations.literal: Later, because of his status as an imperial relative, his treatment grew still more generous and he was transferred to General-in-Chief of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because of his status as an imperial relative, his treatment grew still more generous and he was made General-in-Chief of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及河南王妃罪廢，弘升亦免官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Henan's consort was deposed for an offense, Hongsheng was also removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Henan's consort was deposed for an offense, Hongsheng was also removed from office.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，曆冀州刺史、信都太守，進位金紫光祿大夫，轉涿郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he successively served as Governor of Ji Prefecture and Administrator of Xindu, was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was transferred to Administrator of Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he successively served as Governor of Ji Prefecture and Administrator of Xindu, was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was transferred to Administrator of Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，檢校左武衛大將軍事，指平壤。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign he provisionally oversaw the affairs of Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and advanced toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he provisionally oversaw the affairs of Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and advanced toward Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 與宇文述等同敗績，奔還，發病而卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: He was defeated together with Yuwen Shu and the others, fled back, fell ill and died at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated together with Yuwen Shu and the others, fled back, fell ill and died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: ○元弘嗣

translations.literal: ○ Yuan Hongsi
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi

sentences.zh: 元弘嗣，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongsi was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖剛，魏漁陽王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gang was Prince of Yuyang of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gang was Prince of Yuyang of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父經，周漁陽郡公。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Duke of Yuyang Commandery of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was Duke of Yuyang under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 弘嗣少襲爵，十八為左親衛。

translations.literal: Hongsi in youth inherited the title; at eighteen he was Left Imperial Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsi inherited the title in youth and at eighteen became Left Imperial Guard Attendant.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，從晉王平陳，以功授上儀同。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang he followed the Prince of Jin in pacifying Chen and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang he followed the Prince of Jin in pacifying Chen and was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除觀州總管長史，在州專以嚴峻任事，吏人多怨之。
