translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Chief Administrator of Guanzhou; in the province he relied solely on severity in affairs, and many among the clerks resented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became Chief Administrator of Guanzhou and governed solely by severity, earning much resentment among his staff.

sentences.zh: 二十年，轉幽州總管長史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 于時燕榮為總管，肆虐于弘嗣，每被笞辱。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Rong was General-in-Chief; he tyrannized Hongsi and Hongsi was often beaten and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yan Rong was general-in-chief and tyrannized Hongsi, who was often beaten and humiliated.

sentences.zh: 弘嗣心不伏，榮遂禁弘嗣於獄，將殺之。

translations.literal: Hongsi's heart would not submit; Rong then imprisoned Hongsi and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsi refused to submit; Rong imprisoned him and was about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 及榮誅死，弘嗣為政，酷又甚之。

translations.literal: When Rong was executed and died, Hongsi took power; his cruelty was still worse.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was executed, Hongsi took power—and his cruelty surpassed Rong's.

sentences.zh: 每推鞫囚徒，多以酢灌鼻，或襜弋其下竅，無敢隱情，奸偽屏息。

translations.literal: Whenever he interrogated prisoners he often poured vinegar into their nostrils or stuffed their lower orifices with felt; none dared conceal facts, and treachery and falsehood were silenced.
translations.idiomatic: In interrogations he often poured vinegar into prisoners' nostrils or stuffed their lower orifices; none dared hide the truth, and fraud ceased.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，授木工監，修營東都。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou he was appointed Director of the Carpentry Office to construct and manage the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Renshou he was appointed Director of the Carpentry Office to build the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 大業初，煬帝潛有取遼東之意，遣弘嗣往東萊海口監造船。

translations.literal: In early Daye the emperor secretly intended to take Liaodong and sent Hongsi to the Donglai seaport to supervise shipbuilding.
translations.idiomatic: In early Daye the emperor secretly planned an expedition to Liaodong and sent Hongsi to Donglai to supervise shipbuilding.

sentences.zh: 諸州役丁苦其捶楚，官人督役，晝夜立于水中，略不敢息，自腰以下，無不生蛆，死者十三四。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers of the prefectures suffered under his beatings; officials supervising labor stood day and night in the water, scarcely daring to rest; from the waist down none failed to grow maggots, and thirteen or fourteen in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: The conscript laborers suffered under his beatings; overseers stood day and night in the water; from the waist down maggots bred, and thirteen or fourteen in ten died.

sentences.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎，轉殿內少監。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and transferred to Junior Director of the Palace Interior.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Junior Director of the Palace Interior.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝複征遼東，會奴賊寇隴右，詔弘嗣擊之。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again campaigned in Liaodong; it happened that slave bandits raided Longyou, and an edict ordered Hongsi to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor campaigned in Liaodong again; when slave bandits raided Longyou, Hongsi was ordered to attack them.

sentences.zh: 及玄感作亂，逼東都，弘嗣屯兵安定。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and pressed the eastern capital, Hongsi garrisoned troops at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and threatened the eastern capital, Hongsi garrisoned Anding.

sentences.zh: 或告之謀應玄感者，代王侑遣使執之，送行在所。

translations.literal: Someone reported that he plotted to join Xuangan; the Prince of Dai You sent men to seize him and escort him to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused him of plotting with Xuangan; the Prince of Dai sent men to seize him and escort him to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 以無反形當釋，帝疑不解，除名，徙日南，道死，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Because there was no sign of rebellion he should have been released; the emperor suspected and would not resolve it, struck his name, and exiled him to Rinan; he died on the road, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: With no evidence of rebellion he should have been released, but the emperor remained suspicious, struck his name, and exiled him to Rinan; he died on the road at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 有子仁觀。

translations.literal: He had a son Renguan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Renguan.

sentences.zh: ○王文同

translations.literal: ○ Wang Wentong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentong

sentences.zh: 王文同，京兆潁陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wentong was a man of Yingyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentong was a native of Yingyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 性明辯，有幹用。

translations.literal: His nature was clear in debate and possessed practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was sharp in debate and capable in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，以軍功拜儀同，尋授桂州司馬。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang for military merit he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience; soon he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience for military merit, then Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，征為光祿少卿，以忤旨，出為恆山郡丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; for offending the emperor's intent he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; for offending the throne he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 有一人豪猾，每持長吏長短，前後守令鹹憚之。

translations.literal: There was one man, fierce and cunning, who always held the senior officials' faults and shortcomings; former and later governors and magistrates all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce local bully always held officials' weaknesses over them; successive governors and magistrates all feared him.

sentences.zh: 文同下車，聞其名，召而數之。

translations.literal: When Wentong descended from his carriage he heard the name and summoned and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Wentong heard of him, summoned him, and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 因令左右剡木為大橛，埋之於庭，出尺餘，四角各埋小橛。

translations.literal: He then ordered his attendants to carve a great stake of wood, buried it in the courtyard with more than a chi exposed, and at the four corners buried small stakes each.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants carve a great wooden stake, buried it in the courtyard with more than a chi exposed, and set four smaller stakes at the corners.

sentences.zh: 令其人踣心於木橛上，縛四支於小橛，以棒毆其背，應時潰爛。

translations.literal: He made the man lie chest-down on the great stake, bound his four limbs to the small stakes, and beat his back with a club until it promptly putrefied and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He laid the man chest-down on the great stake, bound his limbs to the small stakes, and beat his back until it burst open.

sentences.zh: 郡中大駭，吏人相視懾氣。

translations.literal: The whole commandery was greatly terrified; clerks and people looked at one another in cowed spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The whole commandery was terrified; officials and commoners looked on one another in dread.

sentences.zh: 及帝征遼東，令文同巡察河北諸郡。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he ordered Wentong to inspect the commanderies of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he ordered Wentong to inspect the Hebei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 文同見沙門齋戒菜食者，以為妖妄，皆收系獄。

translations.literal: Wentong, seeing Buddhist monks observing fasts and eating vegetables, considered it demonic delusion and all were seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing monks on vegetarian fasts, he judged them deluded and had them all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 比至河間，召諸郡官人，小有遲違者，輒皆覆面於地而箠殺之。

translations.literal: Reaching Hejian he summoned the commandery officials; those with the slightest delay were all turned face-down on the ground and clubbed to death.
translations.idiomatic: At Hejian he summoned the commandery officials; anyone slightly tardy was thrown face-down and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 求沙門相聚講論，及長老共為佛會者數百人，文同以為聚結惑眾，盡斬之。

translations.literal: Seeking monks gathered to lecture and elders jointly holding Buddhist assemblies—several hundred persons—Wentong considered it gathering to delude the masses and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Finding several hundred monks gathered for lectures and Buddhist assemblies, he judged them sedition and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 又悉裸僧尼，驗有淫狀非童男女者數千人，複將殺之。

translations.literal: He also stripped all monks and nuns bare and examined them; several thousand who showed signs of licentious conduct and were not chaste boys and girls he was again about to kill.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped monks and nuns and examined them; several thousand who were not chaste he prepared to kill as well.

sentences.zh: 郡中士女號哭于路，諸郡驚駭，各奏其事。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and ladies of the commandery wailed along the roads; the commanderies were all alarmed and each memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wailed in the streets; alarmed commanderies each reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而大怒，遣使者達奚善意馳鎖之，斬於河間，以謝百姓，仇人剖其棺，臠其肉而啖之，斯須鹹盡。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly enraged; he sent envoy Daxi Shanyi post-haste to lock him in chains and behead him at Hejian to appease the people; enemies opened his coffin, sliced his flesh, and ate it—within a moment all was gone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, sent envoy Daxi Shanyi to seize and behead him at Hejian to appease the people; enemies opened his coffin, carved his flesh, and devoured it until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：禦之良者，不在於煩策，政之善者，無取於嚴刑。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The good at governing lies not in numerous policies; the good in administration takes nothing from severe punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Good governance does not lie in multiplying policies; sound administration does not rely on harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 故雖寬猛相資，德刑互設，然不嚴而化，前哲所重。

translations.literal: Therefore though leniency and severity mutually assist, virtue and punishment are set in turn, yet transformation without severity is what former sages valued.
translations.idiomatic: Though leniency and severity may complement each other and virtue and punishment alternate, the sages valued transforming people without relying on severity.

sentences.zh: 士文等運屬欽明，時無桀黠，未閑道德，實懷殘忍。

translations.literal: Shiwen and the like met a time of reverent clarity when there were no fierce villains; unacquainted with moral power, they truly harbored cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Shiwen lived in an age of enlightened rule without fierce villains; ignorant of moral power, they truly harbored cruelty.

sentences.zh: 賊人肌體，同諸木石，輕人性命，甚於芻狗。

translations.literal: They flayed men's flesh as if it were wood and stone, and held human life lighter than grass and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: They flayed human flesh as though it were wood and stone and valued life less than straw dogs.

sentences.zh: 長惡不悛，鮮有不及，故或身嬰罪戮，或憂恚顛隕。

translations.literal: Long in wickedness and unrepentant, few failed to come to ruin—therefore some personally suffered punishment and execution, or died of grief and resentment in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Persisting in wickedness without repentance, few escaped ruin—some were punished and executed, others died of grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，以為有天道焉。

translations.literal: All the gentlemen considered that there was Heaven's Way in it.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle took this as proof that Heaven's justice still operated.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ah—alas!

sentences.zh: 後來之士，立身從政，縱不能為子高門以待封，其可令母掃墓而望喪乎？

translations.literal: Scholars who come after, in establishing themselves and engaging in government—even if they cannot be like Zi Gao with his gate awaiting enfeoffment—how can they allow their mothers to sweep graves while watching for funeral processions?
translations.idiomatic: For those who follow, in taking up office and public life: even if one cannot rise like Zi Gao with honor waiting at one's gate, must one reduce one's mother to sweeping the grave and watching for the funeral train?
